docs.title: Runaria Wiki
docs.text: Everything Runaria adds on top of Minecraft — how each system works, what the commands are, and where to find things. Use the search bar at the top if you already know what you're looking for.

docs.title: New here? Start with these
docs.text:
Runaria is a full RPG server. The five systems you'll touch on day one:

  • Classes — 44 of them. Pick a base class, promote at level 30, unlock the rest with Class Tokens.
  • Traits — permanent passive bonuses you earn just by playing.
  • Quests — a story line that teaches the server, plus a daily quest board and its own shop.
  • Guilds — free to create, and the gateway to land claims, upgrades, and guild contracts.
  • Professions — ten of them, and they level your character too.
  • Cooking — four stations, 120 dishes, and food that carries the cook's name.

docs.title: Anomaly Zones
docs.text: Temporary zones that appear in the wild, announce themselves server-wide, and vanish again. Some boost you — some want you dead.

docs.title: The five anomalies
docs.text:
Anomaly Type What happens inside Azure Bloom Farming Crop growth ×2, harvest yield ×1.5, farming EXP ×1.5 — 30 min Verdant Surge EXP Vanilla, class, and profession EXP ×1.5 — 30 min Crimson Rift Invasion Waves of event mobs; every 15 kills earns you a personal Crimson Cache that spawns near you Eclipse Rift Boss A boss awakens when the first player enters; killing it drops 2–5 public loot caches, then the rift collapses True Eclipse Rift PvP Boss Same as Eclipse, but PvP is forced inside — and the boss drops 5–10 caches

Azure Bloom, Verdant Surge, and Crimson Rift are guaranteed to appear at least every 2 hours. The two Eclipse rifts run on a 4-hour guarantee.

docs.title: Finding them
docs.text:
• Server broadcasts warn 10, 5, and 1 minute before a zone spawns, and again when it moves or despawns.
  • Zones show on the web map as coloured circles.
  • /anomalys lists every live zone with location, radius, time left, and PvP status. Right-click an entry to point your compass at it.
  • Inside a zone you'll see a boss bar, particles, and an entry title. Zones relocate periodically, so keep an eye on the broadcasts.

docs.title: Loot caches
docs.text:
Caches glow until opened and cannot be broken, hoppered, or blown up.

  • Crimson caches are yours alone — nobody else can open one that spawned for you. If a cache is pending, /az claim gives it to you.
  • Eclipse caches are public — first come, first served after the boss dies.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does /anomalys List active anomaly zones (aliases /anomalies, /activeanomalies) /az claim Claim a pending owner-only cache

docs.title: Bestiary
docs.text: Runaria replaces most of what you'd expect to meet in the world. This is what's out there, where it lives, and what's worth killing.

docs.title: Progression at a glance
docs.text:
The server's own experience values rank the fight ladder like this:

Enderling → Ender Watchman → End Strider → Temple Skeletons → Lich King → Cog Sentinel

docs.title: The End frontier
docs.text:
An End-themed area out in the overworld, and the best material farm in the game. This is where new adventurers cut their teeth — Mest is stationed there to help.

Creature What it is Enderling A small enderman. Fast, teleports constantly. The safe, reliable grind. End Wraith A small flying spirit that dashes and spin-slashes. Usually summoned, occasionally alone. Ender Watchman A sorcerer with a lantern who summons End Wraiths and shoves with the lantern. Ender Crawler A multi-legged beast with fang, horn and jump attacks. Enderbruiser A heavy brute that smashes and throws players. Endermauler A large screaming horror that teleports periodically and closes with slash flurries. Ender Strider "Quite slow, but pack a powerful punch." The prize of the zone.

docs.title: What they drop
docs.text:
Enderlings give Teleport Dust, Deep Pearls and Void Crystals — the reagents behind every gemstone and enchant stone you'll ever craft. Watchmen, Crawlers and Endermaulers add Void Fabric, Ender Carapace, Heart of Ender and rarer void materials.

End Striders are several times more productive than anything else here, dropping those same reagents in bulk, and they're the only source of the Ancient Key that opens Temple.

You can ride one

Ender Striders are tameable. Feed one a Golden Apple — roughly a one-in-three chance per apple — and it gains a saddle. They carry a passenger, too.

docs.title: Temple undead
docs.text:
Found only inside Temple.

  • Skeleton Warrior — "A weak skeletal grunt. They appear plentifully guarding the dungeon, but no one knows why."
  • Skeleton Archer — "Their pride in their skills is unmatched, even though they miss more shots than they hit."
  • Skeleton Shaman — a skeletal caster. The Codex hints these may be what animates the Cog Sentinel.
  • Lich King — "He used to command a great army before ending up trapped in the dungeon. No one knows how he got there." A robed skeletal caster who fights with a scythe and shadow magic.
  • Cog Sentinel — "No one knows how this assortment of gears gained sentience." A towering clockwork guardian that fires tracking projectiles which scorch the floor and detonate. The highest-experience kill on the server.

docs.title: The cult
docs.text:
A ritual-themed group you'll only meet somewhere well off the beaten path. If you've run into these, you found something.

  • Cultist — hits hardest of the group in raw melee.
  • Berserk — a hulking, slow-swinging brute.
  • Monster — a fast charging mass.
  • Sorcerer — mixes melee with ranged spellcasting.
  • Lich — a floating caster that keeps its distance, panics away from you, and leaves orbs behind.

Cultists and Berserks carry Dark Soul Sand; Monsters and Liches carry Smouldering Ash. Both are gemcrafting materials you can't get anywhere else.

Something considerably worse than any of them waits at the end.

docs.title: The Deep Dark
docs.text:
Sculk creatures spawn naturally in Deep Dark biomes. They're capped tightly so you'll meet them one or two at a time.

  • Echo Enshrouder — the heavyweight. Soul explosions, sculk spikes, blankets the area in darkness, fires from both hands. The rarest of the group.
  • Sculk Sentinel — a grappler that grabs, smashes, stomps and lashes with its tongue.
  • Sculk Screamer — screams the moment it enters combat. Expect company.
  • Sculked Crustacean and Sculk Crabby — pinching swarm creatures.
  • Soul Bearer — a ranged shooter.

They drop nothing

None of the sculk creatures drop anything at all. Fight them to clear a path or for the challenge, not for profit.

docs.title: Ocean life
docs.text:
A full marine ecosystem spawns across the oceans, split by water temperature.

Gentle Ocean — Catfish, Dolphin, Jellyfish, Lobster, Manatee, Manta Ray, Sea Slug, Seabass, Shark, Spider Crab, Starfish, Sunfish, Swordfish

Exotic Seas (warm and lukewarm) — Betta Fish, Blue Glaucus, Clownfish, Crab, Dory Fish, Electric Eel, Garden Eel, Lionfish, Mahi Mahi, Mantis Shrimp, Narwhal, Oarfish, Ocean Snail, Seahorse, Tropical Fish

Dangerous Deeps (cold, frozen and deep) — Anglerfish, Barracuda, Box Jellyfish, Giant Squid, Hammerhead Shark, Nautilus, Octopus, Orca, Pearl Clam, Piranha, Pistol Shrimp, Pufferfish, Sea Angel, Stingray

Bold entries bite back. Sharks, Orcas and Hammerheads are the apex predators — but the Pistol Shrimp is the sleeper threat, tiny and far harder-hitting than anything its size.

Worth hunting: Nautilus for Nautilus Shells, Pearl Clam for diamonds, gold and iron, Octopus for Ink Sacs in bulk, Blue Glaucus for Experience Bottles, Manta Ray for Phantom Membrane.

docs.title: The Menagerie
docs.text:
A realistic-animal ecosystem spawns across the overworld by biome, and it's the backbone of Runaria's hunting quests. Every one of them is peaceful and deals no damage — with one exception.

Where Animals Savanna Antelope, Elephant (spawns as a parade of four), Giraffe, Hippo, Leopard, Rhino, Zebra, Budgies in ten colours Snowy Plains Snow Leopard, Reindeer, Blue Tit, Cardinal, Robin Jungle Chameleon, Koala Swamp Frogs, Capybara Plains Turkey, Capybara Desert Jerboa Taiga & Old Growth Pine Hedgehog Birch Forest Grizzly Bear Beach Flamingo Frozen Ocean Penguin — the most common of the lot by a wide margin Indoors, anywhere Rats — the only animal that spawns inside buildings, and they do it often

The Black Widow

Small, venomous, bites on contact, and deliberately unrestricted — it can turn up in any biome. The only hostile animal in the Menagerie.

docs.title: Trophies
docs.text:
Every animal drops experience plus a species trophy. Common animals give theirs often; the rare ones are worth hunting deliberately.

Easy and frequent — Capybara Pelt, Frog Eyes, Hedgehog Quills, Turkey Feathers, Zebra Pelt, Penguin Feathers

Worth chasing — Rhino Horn (the rarest at roughly 1 in 20), Jerboa Tail, Reindeer Horn, Giraffe Pelt, Orca Fin, Rat Tail

Seahorses are the odd one out: they drop their fin almost every time and a full spread of live corals, making them the easiest coral farm on the server.

docs.title: The mines
docs.text: Not creatures exactly — destructible resource nodes that repopulate on their own. See Ores & Materials for what they give and how to break them efficiently.

docs.title: Odds and ends
docs.text:
Snails are harmless, extremely slow critters that squelch when they move, with nine randomised shell colours and slightly randomised size — no two look quite alike. They're very rare, drop nothing, and exist purely as ambience.

Some vanilla mobs hit harder here. Cave Spiders, Wither Skeletons and Giants have boosted health and damage server-wide.

Time of day doesn't matter. No custom creature on Runaria has a day/night, weather or moon-phase spawn condition.

docs.title: Dungeons & Parties
docs.text:
Runaria has two dungeons open right now. One you'll be pointed toward. The other you have to find.

Neither has been cleared yet — every First Clear slot on the leaderboards is still open.

docs.title: Two kinds of dungeon
docs.text:
Instanced dungeons give your group a private copy. You enter by command, the run is yours alone, and it's cleaned up when you finish.

World Dungeons are fixed sites out in the world. You walk in — no command. They run one group at a time on a global cooldown shared by everyone, and the site resets in place.

docs.title: Temple
docs.text:
The first real dungeon, and the one to learn on.

Type Instanced — a private copy for your group Players 1–5, soloable Time limit 30 minutes Cooldown None — you can run it again straight away Boss The Cog Sentinel

docs.title: Getting in
docs.text:
Temple sits behind the Ancient Portal, and the portal needs a key.

End Striders in the End frontier drop the Ancient Key — not often, so expect to work for it. Take the key to the matching Ancient Altar and interact: the altar consumes it and lights the portal. Walk through and you're in.

The portal closes behind you. One key, one run.

Where is it?

Runaria's guides only speak of the portal in rumours, and the wiki isn't going to spoil it. Ask around in-game — someone will point you the right way.

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text:
A guarded temple full of skeletal defenders, with the Lich King waiting partway in and the Cog Sentinel at the end. Between them you'll find a sealed chamber that won't open until you work out what opens it, and an arena that won't let you leave until it's satisfied.

Temple is the only dungeon with checkpoints, and players who fall behind get pulled forward rather than stranded — which is a large part of why it's the right place to start.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text:
• Skeletons drop Scorched Bone reliably, Common Manastones often, and occasionally a Common weapon or armour piece.
  • The Lich King and Cog Sentinel both guarantee crafting materials and a Common piece, with a real chance at Common+.
  • Bone Mimic chests are the treasure worth detouring for — cracked gemstones, diamonds, gold and iron blocks or Ember Stones, and each chest rolls several times. Right-click to open; no key needed.

The Cog Sentinel is also the highest-experience kill on the server.

docs.title: Haunted
docs.text:
Somewhere out there is a second dungeon. Bigger, older, and considerably less forgiving.

Nobody's going to hand you directions. What's known is this: it's a World Dungeon, so you walk into it rather than joining it — and because it's shared, you may not be the only ones down there. There's no time limit, and the site resets on its own schedule rather than yours.

It is substantially harder than Temple. There are no checkpoints. Something unpleasant guards the way in. And the way onward is not obvious — you will have to work out what opens the last door, and the answer is not written down here.

Bring people.

Finding it counts

Locating the entrance registers as a Codex discovery worth 50 XP. That's the game telling you it's meant to be found, not told.

What's worth knowing: the boss at the end drops the best gear-per-kill in the game, and it's the only reliable source of Uncommon-tier equipment. Before you go, pick up Haunted Contracts from Kael so your clearing counts toward bounties — and there's a long-form clear quest, The Long Cull, worth 60,000 coins.

World Dungeon caveat

Traits that shorten dungeon cooldowns don't apply here, because the cooldown is global rather than per-player. Traits that add loot rolls work fine.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. The End frontier. Enderlings are a safe grind; End Striders are the prize — far more materials, and the only source of the Ancient Key. Mest is stationed there to help newcomers.
  2. Run Temple with your key. No cooldown, so re-run it for gear — you'll need a fresh key each time.
  3. Gear up to Common+ off the Lich King and Cog Sentinel.
  4. Go looking for the other one. You'll know when you've found it.

docs.title: Parties
docs.text:
/party opens the party GUI.

  • Parties hold up to 6 players and survive server restarts.
  • Set them Open or Closed. Browse open parties, or post in Looking-For-Players with class and level filters.
  • Member entries show class, level, status, and each member's three fastest runs.
  • Party experience sharing: when any member earns main-class experience from any source, every other online member gets the same full amount, wherever they are. Profession experience is never shared.
  • If your party leader starts a dungeon, everyone gets an opt-in prompt. The run launches once everyone accepts, or after 30 seconds.

docs.title: Inside any dungeon
docs.text:
• A scoreboard tracks elapsed time, lives, players alive, and your current objective.
  • Lives are shared by the party. Dying puts you into a spectator state rather than ending the run — the rest fight on.
  • Loot chests are per-player. Everyone opens the same chest and gets their own roll; chests are never used up.
  • Loot that doesn't fit your inventory is delivered on your next login.
  • Disconnecting gives you 2 minutes to reconnect.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does /dungeon list List dungeons and whether each is playable (alias /dg) /dungeon info <id> Player range, time limit, cooldown /dungeon join <name> Enter an instanced dungeon — party if you lead one /dungeon join Accept a pending party launch /dungeon leave Leave your run, or teleport out of a World Dungeon /party Party GUI (alias /p) /leaderboard First clears and fastest times (alias /lb)

Stuck inside a World Dungeon?

/dungeon leave teleports you to the site's safe exit.

docs.title: PvP & Bounties
docs.text: Open-world PvP is strictly opt-in. Go Rogue to fight other rogues — and rack up a price on your head that anyone can claim.

docs.title: Going rogue
docs.text:
/rogue opens the menu: Go Rogue (with a confirmation screen) and Bounties.

Outside special zones, PvP only works when both players are Rogue or Neutral. Going rogue is broadcast to the server.

You're locked in for 24 hours

Once you go rogue, you can't leave for 24 hours. After that, un-rogueing is instant — unless a bounty sits on you, in which case you enter an 8-hour Neutral state: still killable, bounty still claimable, and you can still fight back. Survive the 8 hours and every player-placed bounty is refunded. Die during it and the un-rogue completes immediately.

  • One free cancel, ever. Every player gets a single instant un-rogue that skips the 24-hour lock. It only works while you're not combat-tagged and not bountied.
  • 15-minute grace. Brand-new rogues can't have player-placed bounties put on them. Automatic bounties ignore this.

docs.title: Bounties
docs.text:
Automatic bounties are funded by the server. Your first triggers after a random 2–9 kills, and every 1–3 kills after that adds another $500–$2,500. When an automatic bounty is claimed, bonus items are also rolled into your death drops.

Player bounties are placed through /bounty:

  • Pick a target, then set money (minimum $100), items, or both. Items are staked in a 27-slot deposit chest and go to whoever claims the bounty.
  • Multiple players can stack contributions on the same head.
  • Placing and claiming are both broadcast.

docs.title: Combat rules
docs.text:
Combat tag lasts 60 seconds and applies to both players in any allowed PvP hit. While tagged:

  • No teleports of any kind — commands, plugin warps, ender pearls, chorus fruit, nether and end portals are all blocked.
  • A countdown shows on your action bar.
  • Logging out kills you, and your attacker still gets bounty credit.

docs.title: Free-for-all zones
docs.text:
Inside any Siege Zone, any Dangerous resource drop, or a forced-PvP anomaly, everyone is attackable regardless of rogue status.

Kills in those zones count exactly like rogue kills — they feed your automatic bounty progression even if you never opted into rogue.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does /rogue Open the rogue menu /bounty Open the bounty list directly

docs.title: Resource Drops
docs.text: Meteors, crop patches, supply crates, and rare Grand Drops crash into the world on their own schedule. Mine them, crack them open, fight over them — then the land heals itself as if nothing happened.

docs.title: Drop types
docs.text: Drop Duration What you do Ore / Meteor Drop 20 min Mine the fallen ore — each block takes a few seconds, with a floating progress bar Crop / Herb Drop 20 min Harvest the patch by right-clicking Supply Crate 20 min Unlock the chests Grand Resource Drop 40 min The big one, roughly every 3 hours: mobs spawn, PvP is enabled, and a long-unlock core guards the best loot

docs.title: How rewards work
docs.text:
• Objectives pay out from weighted loot tables — gear, custom items, money, and EXP.
  • Event mobs: loot goes to the top damage dealer.
  • Bosses: the top 3 damage dealers are rewarded, and the results are broadcast. You need at least 15% of the total damage to place.

Dangerous drops

Any drop can spawn Dangerous. A red warning announces it, PvP turns on inside the site, and rewards are doubled with the odds rebalanced toward rare loot. Bring friends or bring caution.

docs.title: Finding drops
docs.text:
Drops use short IDs like METEOR-1042 with names like Corrupted Meteor. They're announced in chat and appear on the web map with a live countdown.

Command What it does /rd active Active drops with coordinates, as a GUI /rd track <id> Direction and distance to a drop /rd compass <id> Point your compass at a drop /rd info <id> Drop details

In the Active Drops GUI: left-click to track, shift-left-click to set your compass, right-click for details.

docs.title: The site itself
docs.text: Everything inside a drop is protected — only the registered objective blocks can be broken. Once the event ends and no players are nearby, the terrain is restored exactly as it was, so drops never permanently scar the world.

docs.title: Siege Zones
docs.text: Control points scattered across the world. Hold one and it pays you loot on a timer — but everyone inside is fair game.

docs.title: Taking a zone
docs.text:
Capturing an empty zone: stand in the capture point for 60 seconds. The first to finish takes it.

Taking an owned zone: owned zones cannot be timer-captured. Entering one as an enemy wakes the zone boss and its minions. Whichever side deals the most boss damage takes the zone when it dies. If nobody kills the boss within 15 minutes, the zone resets to unclaimed instead.

When a zone changes hands, the previous owner's boss and minions are cleared, so new owners never inherit defenders.

docs.title: Holding a zone
docs.text:
• After a zone changes hands there's a 60-minute cooldown before it can flip again.
  • A zone auto-unclaims after 60 minutes with no owner member online.
  • Zone ownership shows on the web map. Boss spawns, captures, and losses are all announced.

docs.title: The reward vault
docs.text:
Each zone has a linked chest that becomes a paginated vault with unlimited storage — loot accrues into it on a timer while you hold the zone, and never overflows onto the ground.

Collect often

When a zone is taken by a different owner, the vault is wiped down to 9 items. Rare items get first claim on those slots, rarest first, and the rest are topped up with the most recent normal items. Everything else is gone.

First-time capture of an unclaimed zone does not trigger this.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
There are none — you capture by standing your ground and fighting.

Note that everyone inside a siege zone is attackable regardless of rogue status, and kills there count toward automatic bounty progression.

docs.title: Bots
docs.text: Placeable mini-robots that automate the grind: farming, planting, collecting, cooking, and smelting. Each family comes in six rarities, from Common up to Unique.

docs.title: Placing and managing
docs.text:
• Place a bot like any item. It appears as a small robot — by default wearing the face of whoever placed it.
  • Right-click to open its menu. Sneak + right-click to pick it back up (empty its storage first).
  • Bots wander up to 6 blocks from where you set them.
  • Each bot floats a status tag showing what it's doing with a countdown: "Harvesting 4s", "Planting 6s", "Collecting…".
  • In the menu you can collect loot, rename the bot, change its head to any skin, and pick it up.

Placement limits

You can have 10 bots at once. Bots must be placed inside your own guild's claim, and each guild has a shared cap of 5 + Mechanized Workforce upgrade level + (members ÷ 3).

docs.title: Farm bots
docs.text:
Walk a lane, dwell on each block to harvest a strip, and turn around at the field edge. They harvest custom crops (which replant themselves) and vanilla wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, and nether wart — breaking then re-seeding those.

Tier Walk speed Harvest time Reach each side Bonus crops Common 1.5 b/s 8.0s 0 — Uncommon 2.0 b/s 6.0s 1 — Rare 2.5 b/s 4.5s 2 +1 Epic 3.0 b/s 3.0s 3 +1 Legendary 3.5 b/s 2.0s 4 +2 Unique 4.0 b/s 1.5s 5 +3

Legendary and Unique farm bots are season-aware: with one in-game day left in a season they fully harvest the field, bank the seeds, and replant the next season's crop from their seed bag.

docs.title: Planter bots
docs.text:
Patrol a field and fill empty tilled farmland from their seed bag. At season end they break the current crop and replant for the next season.

Every planter tier is season-aware. Their storage grid is the seed bag — click a stack to withdraw, click or shift-click to deposit, or use the "Empty seed bag" button. They also vacuum loose seeds within 6 blocks and get first claim on dropped seeds over a collector.

docs.title: Collection bots
docs.text:
Epic and above only. Stationary vacuums that pull ground items into storage, with per-category toggles for seeds, produce, and other.

Tier Coverage Epic 1 chunk Legendary 3×3 = 9 chunks Unique 5×5 = 25 chunks

Seeds are handed to a nearby planter first. Farm bots inside a collector's coverage drop their haul for the collector instead of banking it themselves.

docs.title: Cooking bots
docs.text:
One bot per cooking station — prep, chopping, stove and oven — each in six rarities. Pick a recipe in the bot's menu, feed it ingredients by hand or by hopper, and it cooks with your Cooking level and your ingredient quality, exactly as if you'd stood there yourself.

  • It has to stand next to a real station of its own type, within about five blocks.
  • One cook at a time. The bot queues for the station like anyone else, and it loses to a player.
  • It can only cook what you've discovered. A bot is no way around the recipe book.
  • Cooking experience comes back at half rate, and is held for you if you're offline.

Rarity buys reliability, not just speed

Cheap bots are sloppy — they burn food, come up short, and fumble their cuts. Expensive ones rarely do. Rarity also gates recipes: below Epic a bot is capped at its own rarity, while an Epic or better bot can attempt anything up to Unique — but each tier above its own takes far longer.

docs.title: Smelting bots
docs.text:
Auto-craft a chosen smelting recipe with your profession scaling, quality stamps, and profession EXP — exactly as if you'd made it by hand at the station.

  • Smelting bots discover every recipe with an ingot output.
  • A bot only offers recipes whose output tier is at or below its own rarity.

docs.title: Hopper support
docs.text: A bot standing on a hopper unloads its storage into it. A hopper directly above a bot feeds it — seeds go to a planter's seed bag, everything else to storage.

docs.title: Cooking
docs.text:
Cooking is a profession you do, not a menu you click. You buy stations, place them in your own kitchen, gather produce, and work each dish through the stations it needs. A finished plate carries your name, your Cooking level and the quality of everything that went into it — so two players making the same recipe do not get the same item.

Start with Kate

Kate is Sylari's chef, in the farmhouse and bakery she shares with Keidi. Talk to her to get started — she'll explain the stations, sell you your first one, and tell you what's worth cooking at your level. Everything on these pages, she can walk you through in person.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
1. Buy a station from the Cooking section of the server shop, and place it wherever you like.
  2. Gather ingredients — crops, animal produce, and pantry staples from the shop.
  3. Cook. Each dish is made at one particular station.
  4. Eat it, or sell it. Cooked food is traded through the market, and good food sells.

docs.title: What a dish gives you
docs.text:
Every dish restores hunger, saturation, health and mana. How much depends on its rarity — a Common dish restores less than a basic health potion, while the top of the ladder is in a different league entirely.

On top of that, dishes grant timed stat buffs:

Rarity Buffs Common One stat, briefly Uncommon One stat, for longer Rare Sometimes two stats, or one that runs much longer Epic Same shape as Rare, but stronger and longer — plus a Saturation effect Legendary Always two stats Unique Any number of stats, and very hard to make

The stats themselves span the whole roster — health, mana, damage, defence, crit, movement speed, regeneration and more. A few dishes carry something rarer still: effects that boost profession experience, class experience, dungeon party experience, or the quality of traits you roll, for half an hour at a time. Those are worth saving for the run you actually care about.

docs.title: The cook is baked into the dish
docs.text:
This is the part that makes a good chef valuable.

Whoever eats it gets your numbers

A dish's strength is calculated from the cook's Cooking level at the moment it was made, and then stored in the item. A meal from a master chef is exactly as strong in a brand-new player's hands as it is in theirs.

Which is the whole argument for having a dedicated cook in your guild — and for buying food from one rather than making your own while you're still levelling.

The item itself tells you the truth: every dish is stamped with who prepared it and at what level, and its lore lists the real numbers that plate will give you.

docs.title: Ingredient quality
docs.text:
Crops come in three grades, and cooking carries that grade all the way through to the plate.

Ingredient Dish becomes Effect Normal produce Ordinary Baseline Silver Star Amazing Stronger Golden Star Perfection Strongest

Quality is proportional, not all-or-nothing — cooking with some starred produce lands you part of the way. It also survives processing: dice a golden-star crop and the result is still golden, so a batter made from good produce bakes into a better cake.

Some recipes go further and demand a grade. A handful of Legendary and Unique dishes will not accept anything below Silver or Golden star, which is what makes them projects rather than recipes. See Farming for how to get starred crops reliably.

docs.title: Levelling
docs.text:
Cooking is one of the ten professions, and it levels from cooking — plus a trickle from harvesting crops, so farmers gain it without trying.

Level does three things:

  • Unlocks recipes. Rare needs 15, Epic 35, Legendary 65, Unique 100.
  • Strengthens everything you cook, in both effect size and duration.
  • Sharpens the timer at the stove and oven. Below level 10 you get a progress bar and nothing else; at 25 the last digit appears; at 60 the seconds are readable; at 100 you see the full countdown. Early cooks learn timing by feel, and veterans read the clock.

docs.title: Prepared ingredients
docs.text:
Four things made at a station aren't dishes — they're components other recipes ask for: Croissant Dough, Pancake Batter, Waffle Batter and Tomato Paste. You'll meet them as soon as you start baking.

Quality carries through

A batter made from starred produce stays starred, and passes that on to whatever you bake with it. See Cooking.

docs.title: The Recipe Book
docs.text: Type /recipes anywhere to open your book. It's your record of everything you've worked out, and your map of everything you haven't.

docs.title: Every recipe has a slot
docs.text:
The book shows all 120 dishes from the moment you open it for the first time. Recipes you haven't discovered sit behind a question mark.

That's deliberate. You can see how much cooking is left to find, and watching the question marks turn into dishes is the progression. What you can't see is what's inside one — the ingredients stay hidden until you've earned them.

docs.title: Discovering recipes
docs.text:
You discover recipes by handling their ingredients. Pick up a crop you've never held, and every recipe that uses it moves a step closer to being readable.

Discovery cascades

Ingredients are shared across dozens of dishes, so learning one new crop lights up parts of a whole line of recipes at once. Farming widely is the fastest way to fill the book — a season spent growing something new usually unlocks more than a season spent cooking.

A recipe becomes fully readable once you know everything that goes into it. Until then you'll see it partly masked, which is often enough to tell you what you're missing.

Recipes can also be granted outright. Some quests hand you one as a reward, so a dish you'd never have stumbled on can arrive complete.

docs.title: Cooking from the book
docs.text:
Open the book while standing at a Prep Station and each recipe gains a Move Ingredients button. It pulls the ingredients out of your inventory and puts them on the board for you.

It only fills a board it can fill: if you're short, it says so rather than half-loading the grid, and a 4×4 recipe won't transfer onto a 3×3 board.

docs.title: Recipe paper
docs.text:
Any recipe you know can be copied onto paper — a physical sheet you can trade, sell or hand to a friend, and which teaches whoever uses it.

Two rules worth knowing:

  • You keep the recipe. Copying doesn't cost you the knowledge, only a sheet of paper. Nobody ever accidentally sells the only copy of something they spent a season discovering.
  • One copy per recipe. You can't print a Unique dish forever and flood the market with it.

That makes rare recipes a genuine trade good. If you're the first person on the server to work out a Legendary dish, that sheet is worth something to someone.

docs.text: Command What it does /recipes Open your recipe book (aliases /recipe, /cookbook)

docs.title: The Four Stations
docs.text:
Cooking happens at furniture you own and place yourself. There are four stations, each doing a different job, and most dishes pass through more than one of them.

Buy them from the Cooking section of the server shop, or ask Kate — she keeps them in stock.

Station What it does Cost Prep Station Assembled meals: sandwiches, bowls, sushi, doughs 25,000 Chopping Station Dicing and juicing raw produce 15,000 Kitchen Stove Timed cooking: stews, fries, curries, meats 50,000 Kitchen Oven Timed baking: breads, cakes, pastries, jellies 85,000

docs.title: Prep Station
docs.text:
The kitchen island. Right-click it and it asks what you're making:

  • Small Meal — a 3×3 board
  • Large Meal — a 4×4 board

Both live in the same piece of furniture, so you only ever need one.

Prep recipes are shapeless: put the right ingredients anywhere on the board and the dish assembles. What you're discovering is what goes in, not where it sits.

It's still exact, though — the board has to hold the recipe's ingredients and nothing else. A stray item in a corner stops the match rather than silently getting eaten.

Let the book fill the board

Open the recipe book at a prep station, pick a recipe, and press Move Ingredients. It pulls everything straight out of your inventory onto the board in one click.

docs.title: Chopping Station
docs.text:
The kitchen counter. One ingredient in, a processed one out — diced vegetables, juices, pastes.

Chopping is the one station with a minigame. A marker sweeps across a track and you click while it's inside the green window. Land it and the cut counts; land four and the job's done.

You always have a choice:

How Yield Experience Time the cuts Full Full Quick chop Much less Much less

The quick chop exists because timing forty cucumbers is tiring. Use it when you're processing bulk and take the timed cut when the ingredient is worth it.

A knife in your inventory raises the yield by half again — see Knives & Tools.

docs.title: Kitchen Stove and Kitchen Oven
docs.text:
The two timed stations. Load the ingredients, start it, and wait. A floating readout above the station shows a progress bar and, depending on your Cooking level, a countdown.

Food burns

When a dish finishes it does not wait for you indefinitely. Leave it too long and it burns — you get a ruined item, or nothing at all. Stay nearby and collect it.

A higher Cooking level buys you a longer grace period, on top of a clearer timer.

Surplus is fine. A stack of flour bakes one loaf and keeps the rest, the way a furnace smelts one ore at a time — you don't have to count out exact amounts. What the station won't accept is an ingredient the recipe has no use for.

The stove handles savoury cooking: stews, soups, fried and grilled meats, curries, drinks. The oven handles everything baked: breads, cakes, pastries, ice creams and jellies. The oven is the larger investment and it holds the bulk of the high-rarity menu.

docs.title: Owning a station
docs.text:
Stations are yours. You buy the furniture, place it wherever you like, and break it to pick it back up.

  • Private by default. Only you can cook at a station you placed.
  • You can open it up. Toggle a station public and anyone may use it — handy for a guild kitchen or a town square.
  • Some stations are public already. Staff-placed stations around the world belong to nobody and are open to everyone. If you're not ready to buy, look for one of those.
  • One cook at a time. A station in use is a station in use. Walk up to a busy oven and you'll be told to wait your turn.

That last rule matters more than it sounds, because it also applies to bots: a cooking bot has to queue for the station like anybody else, and it loses to a player.

docs.title: Knives & Tools
docs.text: Cooking tools are held items. You don't equip them or slot them into a station — you simply carry one, and the station notices. They're sold in the Cooking section of the server shop alongside the stations.

docs.title: What a tool does
docs.text:
Carrying the right tool for a job gives you half again the yield, and costs the tool a point of durability.

Tools wear out

These have real durability and they break. A knife used for a few hundred cuts is finished. Budget for replacements, or keep a spare in your kitchen.

No recipe currently requires a tool — you can cook badly on day one and upgrade into competence. Working without one just means smaller yields.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text: Tool Cost What it's for Paring Knife 2,500 The cheap knife. Does the job. Bread Knife 3,500 Long serrated blade. Kitchen Knife 5,000 A proper chef's knife. Cleaver 8,000 Heavy blade for bone and joint work. Cutting Board 4,000 A steady surface to work on. Rolling Pin 4,000 Flattens dough. Grater 4,500 Shreds and zests. Meat Tenderiser 6,000 Beats meat flat before cooking.

docs.title: Knives
docs.text:
All four knives do the same job — they're what the Chopping Station looks for. Every chopping recipe in the game is a dicing job, and any knife satisfies it.

The difference between them is how long they last, not how well they work. A Paring Knife and a Cleaver produce identical results; the Cleaver simply survives far more cuts before it breaks. Buy the cheap one while you're learning and the expensive one once you're processing crops in bulk.

docs.title: The rest
docs.text:
Boards, pins, graters and tenderisers are ahead of the recipes

These four are stocked and fully functional, but the current recipe list doesn't call for them yet — every chopping job is a knife job. They're there for the recipes still being added, and they'll start earning their keep as the chopping menu grows.

Buy a knife first. Come back for these when there's something to use them on.

docs.title: What to buy first
docs.text:
A Paring Knife, and nothing else. It's 2,500, it covers every chopping recipe in the game, and half again on yield pays for itself quickly once you're juicing and dicing at any volume.

Move up to a Kitchen Knife or Cleaver when replacing knives starts to feel like a chore rather than an expense.

docs.title: Backpacks
docs.text: Backpacks are real items with real stats: paginated storage you carry anywhere, plus passive buffs while the pack rides in your offhand.

docs.title: Using a backpack
docs.text:
• Right-click to open. Works from either hand. If you're aiming at a chest or door, sneak first so the block doesn't win the click.
  • Contents are stored server-side, so they survive anything that happens to your inventory.
  • Storage paginates at 45 slots per page, up to a maximum of 450 slots (10 pages). Unearned slots on the last page show as locked.

Offhand buffs

Every stat rolled on a backpack applies while you hold it in your offhand — max health, mana, defense, movement speed, cooldown reduction and more. A backpack isn't just storage; it's a gear slot.

Ten backpacks ship from Common to Legendary, ranging 18–90 slots, each with its own themed stat spread.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Visit the Backpack NPC to upgrade your pack. The ladder runs:

Common → Common+ → Uncommon → Uncommon+ → Rare → Rare+ → Epic → Epic+ → Legendary → Legendary+ → Unique

Each step adds a rolled range of bonus slots and costs progressively more:

Step Cost Common+ 25,000 Uncommon 45,000 Uncommon+ 81,000 Rare 146,000 Rare+ 262,000 Epic 472,000 Epic+ 850,000 Legendary 1,530,000 Legendary+ 2,754,000 Unique 4,957,000

Your rolls are preserved

A well-rolled backpack stays well-rolled through every upgrade. If your main stat rolled at 45.7% of its band, it's still at 45.7% of the new, higher band after upgrading — you're never punished for upgrading a good pack.

Gem sockets: reaching each main rarity has a 50% chance to add an uncoloured gem socket, up to 6 total including the one rolled at creation. The "+" half-tiers give slots and stats but no socket roll.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• No backpacks inside backpacks.
  • Only one player can have a given backpack open at a time.
  • The pack you're holding is frozen while its menu is open.
  • Shift-click deposits merge across every page.

docs.title: Crafting & Item Quality
docs.text: What you craft carries your name — and your skill. Every station craft is stamped with who made it, their profession level, and a quality grade that improves as they level.

docs.title: The Forged-By stamp
docs.text:
Weapons, armor, tools, and gemstones crafted at stations carry a stamp showing the crafter, their profession level, the grade, and the craft date.

Grades climb with profession level:

Level Grade 1–24 Crude 25–49 Rough 50–74 Sturdy 75–99 Fine 100–124 Superior 125–149 Exquisite 150–174 Masterwork 175–199 Pristine 200 Flawless

Gear stats scale with the crafter's Blacksmithing level. Gem crafts scale with Gemforging, and gemstone success rates gain +1% per 20 profession levels (+10% at level 200).

Buy from good crafters

Because the stamp records who made an item and stats scale off their level, gear from a high-level blacksmith is genuinely better than the same recipe made by a beginner. It's worth checking the stamp before you buy.

docs.title: Refining bonus ingots
docs.text:
Every refinery craft rolls for extra ingots, and the odds scale hard with Blacksmithing level:

  • Level 1 — about a 52% chance of +1
  • Level 25 — +1 guaranteed
  • Level 50 — +1 guaranteed, plus a coin flip for +2
  • Level 100 — +2 guaranteed, plus a coin flip for +3
  • Level 200 — +4 guaranteed, plus a coin flip for +5

When a bonus lands you get a chat line describing the lucky pour. Ingots are never stamped, so they stay clean and stackable.

docs.title: Cooking
docs.text:
Food is only as good as the cook. A dish's strength and duration are calculated from the cook's Cooking level at the moment it's made and then stored in the item, so a meal from a master chef is exactly as strong in a beginner's hands.

Ingredient quality stacks on top of that: cook with starred produce and the dish inherits it. Full detail in Cooking.

docs.title: Gemforging enchant stones
docs.text:
One gem item covers an entire enchant family — the level (I, II, III…) is rolled at craft time from your Gemforging level and shown on the gem's lore. Socketing it applies the real enchantment.

  • Below level 75, the highest tier you can roll rises steadily with your level.
  • Above 75, the odds curve increasingly favours high rolls, all the way to level 200.
  • Gemforging EXP from a craft scales with the rolled level, your own level, and how good the roll was — a perfect roll is worth 50% more EXP.

docs.title: Mystery recipes
docs.text:
Forge and armory recipes with randomised outputs display as clean "Random Epic Helmet"-style entries rather than spoiling the exact roll you'd get.

Each masked recipe still shows you:

  • the base stats for that item type and rarity,
  • the roll summary — how many stats, their power ranges, enchant sockets, and gem quality,
  • a live ingredient checklist, green when you have the item and red when you don't.

Nothing about crafting itself changes — only the display.

docs.title: Gems & Enchanting
docs.text:
Two socketable systems share one starting point. Both begin at the Apothecary, and both are powered by your Gemforging profession.

Kiko runs all of it — every station on this page is opened by talking to her.

Apothecary  →  Gem Catalyst  ─┬─→  Gem Station    →  stat gemstones
                              └─→  Enchant Forge  →  enchant stones

The Apothecary's single recipe consumes only dungeon reagents, so gem crafting is gated behind dungeon running rather than mining.

docs.title: Gemstones
docs.text: Four families, five quality grades each — twenty gemstones, all crafted at the Gem Station. Talk to Kiko.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
Grade Rarity Cracked Common Polished Uncommon Radiant Rare Perfect Epic Mythic Legendary

Cracked gems of all four families are craftable from level 1, and also drop from Temple chests. The higher grades unlock much later.

docs.title: Families
docs.text: Family Theme Stats it rolls Ruby Melee and physical Attack damage, attack speed, crit chance and power, PvE/PvP damage, weapon damage Sapphire Caster and ranged Skill crit chance and power, magic damage, projectile damage, cooldown reduction, attack speed Emerald Defence Max health, armor, armor toughness, knockback resistance, movement speed, damage reduction Amethyst Generalist The same offensive spread as Ruby, at roughly 60% of the size. A flexible filler, not a best-in-slot gem.

docs.title: Every gem rolls two extras
docs.text:
Success Rate — the chance the gem actually sockets instead of shattering. Most gems roll somewhere between 25% and 75%, but one in ten rolls Lucky (75–100%) and one in ten rolls Unlucky (1–25%).

Check the success rate before you socket

An Unlucky gem has as little as a 1% chance of applying. Read the number on the gem before you commit it to gear you care about.

Your Gemforging level helps: +1% success per 20 levels, so +10% at level 200.

Empowered — roughly a one-in-ten chance for a gem to gain the Empowered prefix, which rolls from a separate, tighter stat pool.

docs.title: Sockets
docs.text:
Gear rolls sockets randomly. Accessories — rings, amulets, bracelets, gloves and artifacts — have about a 50% chance of one socket, which will be Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, Amethyst or Uncolored.

An Uncolored socket accepts any gem family, which makes it the most valuable roll.

Use a Gem Remover to pop a gem back out.

docs.title: Enchant Stones
docs.text: Enchant Stones carry an enchantment and socket into an item's Enchant Socket. There are 123 of them — 81 custom Runaria enchantments and 42 vanilla ones.

docs.title: You roll the level, you don't pick it
docs.text:
This is the part that matters most:

  • Below Gemforging 75, you're capped well under an enchant's maximum. At level 1 you will only ever roll level I.
  • At Gemforging 75, every tier becomes reachable.
  • Past 75, the odds keep shifting toward high rolls all the way to level 200.

You also earn bonus Gemforging experience for rolling well — 15% extra at three-quarters of max level, 30% at nine-tenths, and 50% for a perfect maximum roll.

Grind Gemforging before chasing high-level stones

Nothing stops you crafting a top-tier stone at Gemforging 5 — you'll just roll level I and waste the materials. Get to 75 first.

docs.title: Vanilla enchantments, raised
docs.text:
Several vanilla enchantments go above their normal ceiling as stones:

Enchantment Max here Vanilla max Sharpness VIII V Power VIII V Protection VI IV Looting VI III Fortune VI III Unbreaking VI III

docs.title: Custom enchantments
docs.text:
The 81 custom enchantments are also obtainable from enchanting tables, villager trades and loot chests — stones are just the reliable route.

Melee — One for All (+500% damage, but conflicts with every other enchantment), Bleed, Goliath, Lifesteal, Ender Slayer, Cubism, Introversion, Slaughter, Ninja, First Strike, Finishing, Brightness, End and Nether Affinity, Criticals, Abrasion, Fortitude, Shura

Control — Blackout (blind), Confusion (shuffles their hotbar), Stun, Caffeinated, Dexterity

Spells, activated abilities limited to one per item — Charge, Transmission, Ascend, Soul Storm, Rumble, Vitality, Dynamite, Xray

Ranged — Boss Hunter, Wound, Thor (calls lightning), Flashbang, Rapid, Snipe, Frost, Jumpshot, Skull Puncture, Tripleshot, Warp Drive, Contagion, Slipstream

Gathering — Veinminer, Lumberjack (fells a whole tree), Excavation, Blast Mining, Infernal Touch (auto-smelts), Nether Prospector, Telekinesis, Wisdom, Carve

Farming — Replenish (auto-replants), Feather Step (no trampling), Foraging

Defence — Arcane Defence, Thrive, Aura (protects nearby players too), Vanish, Poison Ivy, Haunting, Block Breather, Rebounding, Adrenaline

Movement and utility — Streamlining, Getaway, Escape, Stamina, Metabolism, Rocket Saver, Wyvern, Sparks

Universal — Soulbound (keep the item when you die), Repairing

docs.title: Curses
docs.text:
Curses are craftable too: Breaklessness, Harmlessness, Hunger, Misfortune and Permanence.

Curse of Permanence is irreversible

An item with Curse of Permanence can never be modified in an anvil again. And curses in general cannot be removed with a grindstone.

docs.title: Display rules
docs.text:
• Enchantment descriptions appear in the item's lore, but only while it has five or fewer enchantments.
  • Past nine enchantments the list collapses into compact comma-separated lines.
  • Enchantments above their normal max show in a distinct green gradient.
  • Spell enchantments are limited to one per item — you cannot stack two spells.
  • /enchantinfo opens a menu showing any enchantment's max level, rarity, valid targets and conflicts.

docs.title: The Market
docs.text:
Runaria's entire economy: a server shop, a rotating Black Market, an Auction House, buy/sell orders, player shops, physical storefronts you can own, and the server's second currency — Runaria Coins.

/omnimarket (aliases /om, /market) is the hub menu for all of it.

docs.title: Server Shop
docs.text:
/shop opens the categorised server shop.

  • Build a quantity with +1 / +16 / +64 / Fill Inventory buttons, then confirm once.
  • Blocked purchases always tell you why — out of stock, can't afford, inventory full — rather than just failing.

docs.title: Seed Shop
docs.text:
The seeds category restocks every 3 hours, aligned to 12/3/6/9 o'clock Eastern. A clock in the shop shows the countdown.

  • Only 3–6 seed types are stocked per restock, weighted so common seeds appear far more often than unique ones.
  • Each seed has a per-player purchase limit per cycle.

Crop sell prices climb from 400 (common) to 12,500 (unique) — and star-quality crops multiply that: silver ×5, gold ×11.

docs.title: Junk Vendor
docs.text:
The bottom-right button of /shop. Dump unwanted gear and drops into a 45-slot grid, preview the payout per stack and the running total, then sell it all at once. Anything unsellable is handed back.

Manastones pay best (around 75% of the matching crop price), while old gear sells as vendor trash at roughly 30%. /sell hand and /sell all use the same pricing.

docs.title: Black Market
docs.text: /blackmarket — 9 limited-stock items, rerolled daily at 1:00 AM Eastern from weighted pools, each with its own randomised price and stock. The refresh is broadcast. When it's gone, it's gone.

docs.title: Auction House & Trading Hub
docs.text:
• /ah — list items for other players. Listings last 48 hours, there's no listing fee, and a 5% tax comes off each sale. You get 5 active listings by default, more with rank.
  • /trading — post buy or sell orders at your price and let the market come to you. Orders last up to 7 days by default; 5 active orders, more with rank.
  • /trends — live price trends and 30-day history for traded goods.

docs.title: Player shops
docs.text:
/playershop — rented virtual shops on a 4-tier ladder. Rent scales with how many shops are currently rented server-wide.

Tier Listings Base rent Upgrade cost 1 10 8,000 — 2 20 12,000 25,000 3 35 20,000 75,000 4 50 32,000 200,000

docs.title: Physical storefronts
docs.text:
/store — real buildings you buy or rent from a Realtor NPC, including L-shaped plots.

  • Trust system: assign helpers as Visitor, Builder, Manager, or Co-Owner. Each store also has its own blacklist.
  • Sales: run limited-time discounts on your goods.
  • Upgrades: more trust slots, more categories, longer sale durations, shorter sale cooldowns, custom titles and themes, longer rent grace.
  • Resale & auction: sell or auction your store on. The building and everything in it transfers as-is — blocks, containers, decorations included.
  • /store visit <storeId> unlocks teleports to stores you've found.

You never lose your stock

If a store is evicted or transferred, your listed items move to eviction storage instead of being deleted. Reclaim them with /eviction.

docs.title: Advertising
docs.text: Pay to feature your shop or a specific item, or outbid others for a daily broadcast slot. The top 3 bidders get a featured row plus a rotating chat broadcast every 10 minutes — and their customers get a server-covered 5% discount.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text: Star-rate shops you've actually bought from, on a 24-hour cooldown. Sellers earn badges: Trusted Seller (100 sales at 4.5+), High Volume (1,000 items), Customer Favorite (25 repeat buyers).

docs.title: Money & Runaria Coins
docs.text:
Two currencies

Regular money is what you earn and spend everywhere. Runaria Coins are the premium second currency, earned from gameplay rewards and spent on things like trait upgrades.

Command What it does /shop Server shop (also /servershop, /bazaar) /blackmarket Rotating black market (alias /bm) /ah Auction House (aliases /auction, /auctionhouse) /trading Trading Hub — buy/sell orders (aliases /trade, /hub) /playershop Player shops (aliases /pshop, /ps) /store Storefronts — buy, manage, trust, upgrades, sales, visit /eviction Reclaim items from eviction storage /trends Market analytics and price history /wallet · /balance Your money and Runaria Coins /coins pay <player> <amt> Send Runaria Coins to another player /baltop Money leaderboard /omnimarket Hub menu for everything above

docs.title: Ores & Materials
docs.text:
Runaria has its own metal economy sitting on top of vanilla mining. Twenty-eight raw ores refine into twenty-six metals across four tiers, and everything you craft is made of them.

You cannot strip-mine for these

Custom ores do not generate in the world. No amount of tunnelling will find you Nightsteel. They come from mining nodes, world events, and the market — see below.

docs.title: Mining nodes
docs.text:
The main source. The Sacred Garden mine is where the first tier of ore is dug, and three kinds of node spawn there. Nodes are spread out deliberately, so you can't camp one spot.

Node What it gives Boulder A big pile of one vanilla resource — iron, gold, copper, coal, diamonds, emeralds, redstone, lapis, quartz or netherite scrap. Every boulder is a lottery ticket. Copper Node Raw Mystical Molten Alloy, Froststeel or Abyssium Iron Node Raw Nightsteel, Sunsteel or Starsteel

You must be holding a pickaxe. Any other tool tells you "Can't mine with this tool!" and does nothing. Your pickaxe tier decides how many hits a node takes:

Pickaxe Hits per ore node Wooden 5 Stone 4 Iron 3 Golden 2 Diamond or Netherite 1

There's a half-second cooldown between registered hits, so a diamond pickaxe is a massive throughput upgrade — five times the rate of a wooden one.

More mines are planned for the higher ore tiers.

docs.title: Resource Drops
docs.text: Ore and Meteor Drops crash into the world for 20 minutes at a time and are the best early way to stockpile Ember Stone, alongside a spread of tier-1 raw ores.

docs.title: The market
docs.text: Every raw ore is stocked at the server shop if you'd rather buy than mine.

docs.title: Tier 1 — refined at the Basic Refinery
docs.text:
The early-game backbone. Everything a new player crafts is made from these six.

Ore Colour Raw Nightsteel Deep navy blue Raw Abyssium Dark teal, cyan-green Raw Sunsteel Bright orange-gold Raw Starsteel Blue-and-pink spiked crystal Raw Froststeel Solid deep blue Raw Mystical Molten Alloy Molten red-orange

docs.title: Tier 2 — Advanced Refinery, level 15
docs.text: Raw Bloodsteel (oxblood) · Raw Embersteel (orange) · Raw Cindersteel (ashier reddish-orange) · Raw Crownsteel (purple and gold) · Raw Faesteel (pink and purple plating) · Raw Crystallized Gold (gold shot through with crystal)

docs.title: Tier 3 — Supreme Refinery, level 30
docs.text: Raw Skysteel (sky blue) · Raw Aqualite (bright cyan) · Raw Amethril (bright purple) · Raw Verdanite (green) · Raw Venomsteel (green and purple) · Raw Infected Steel (sickly grey-brown)

docs.title: Tier 4 — Master Refinery, level 45
docs.text:
Raw Bubble Steel (pale mint) · Raw Pearly Steel (iridescent off-white) · Raw Thornsteel (jagged olive) · Raw Soulsteel (violet spirit-metal) · Raw Mechanite (brushed steel-blue) · Raw Nebula Steel (deep violet with starlight) · Raw Dragonsteel (dark burnt red) · Raw Matrix (near-black with a shifting grid)

Dragonsteel and Matrix are the two best metals in the game.

docs.title: Ingots and Big Ingots
docs.text:
Refining happens at the four refineries — talk to Browntul to open them. Every metal exists in two forms, and the difference decides what you can craft.

Ingots are the standard bar, straight from a refinery.

Big Ingots are made at the Basic Refinery: 6 ingots + 2 Ember Stones → 1 Big Ingot. A Big Ingot is always exactly one full rarity above its small version.

Big Ingots are the key to \"+\" gear

Normal gear is crafted from small ingots in bulk — 30 to 42 per item. "+" rarity gear is crafted from Big Ingots, only two to five per item. If you want plus-tier equipment, you need Big Ingots.

Metals Ingot Big Ingot Nightsteel, Abyssium, Sunsteel, Starsteel, Froststeel, Mystical Molten Alloy Common Uncommon Bloodsteel, Embersteel, Cindersteel, Crownsteel, Faesteel, Crystallized Gold Uncommon Rare Skysteel, Aqualite, Amethril, Verdanite, Venomsteel, Infected Steel Rare Epic Bubble Steel, Pearly Steel, Thornsteel, Soulsteel, Mechanite, Nebula Steel Epic Legendary Dragonsteel, Matrix Legendary Unique

docs.title: Reagents
docs.text:
Every refining recipe burns a reagent, and they form a strict chain — which means Ember Stone never becomes obsolete.

Reagent Made at Recipe Ember Stone Basic Refinery 2 Cobblestone + 2 Coal → 4 Blaze Core Advanced Refinery 1 Ember Stone + 1 Blaze Rod + 1 Coal → 8 Fire Essence Supreme Refinery 2 Ember Stone + 2 Blaze Core + 2 Coal Block → 8

Ember Stone also drops from Resource Drops and Temple chests.

docs.title: Dungeon reagents
docs.text:
These come from fighting, not mining, and they're what gate gem and enchant crafting:

Reagent Where Teleport Dust, Deep Pearl, Void Crystal End Striders and Enderlings Common Mana Stone Temple Scorched Bone Temple Dark Soul Sand Cultists and Berserks Smoldering Ash Monsters and Liches

Manastones run their own ladder from Common all the way to Unique.

docs.title: The rarity ladder
docs.text:
Common → Common+ → Uncommon → Uncommon+ → Rare → Rare+ → Epic → Epic+ → Legendary → Legendary+

Tier Colour Common and Common+ Gray Uncommon and Uncommon+ Green Rare and Rare+ Dark Aqua Epic and Epic+ Purple Legendary and Legendary+ Gold

What "+" actually means: a "+" item has the same colour and the same number of stat rolls as its base tier, but each stat's magnitude sits about 30% of the way toward the next full tier. A Rare+ sword genuinely beats a Rare one — but still loses to an Epic.

Break down \"+\" gear, not base gear

Each "+" tier deconstructs into the essence of the tier above it. Deconstructing a Rare+ weapon gives you an Epic Weapon Essence. That makes "+" gear far more efficient to break down than to sell.

Unique exists above Legendary, in red, and is currently reserved for the very best Big Ingots.

docs.title: Other materials
docs.text:
• Weapon Essences — from deconstructing gear. A failed deconstruct instead gives Broken Weapon Powder, and higher tiers lose more of it.
  • Soulbinders and Soulcrushers — Apprentice, Intermediate and Arcane grades. Soulbinders bind an item to you (70%, 80% or 90% success); Soulcrushers break a soulbind.
  • Scroll of Identification — 2 Paper + 1 Diamond. Identifies unidentified drops.
  • Gem Remover and Skin Remover — shears that strip a gem or skin off an item.
  • Restoration Gem — repairs magic items.

docs.title: Crafting Stations
docs.text:
You open crafting stations by talking to the craftsman who runs them. Four NPCs cover everything on the server between them — find the right one, and they'll open the station you need.

Craftsman Handles Velreal Every forge and workbench — all weapons and armor Browntul Every refinery — turning raw ore into ingots Kiko All gem crafting — catalysts, gemstones, enchant stones and ability stones Kate Cooking — she sells the stations rather than opening one

Once a station is open, they all behave the same way: pick a recipe, and the craft goes into a queue of up to ten items that finishes on a timer. Click the queue slot to claim it.

Ranked players can skip the trip

Certain ranks unlock commands that open stations from anywhere, without visiting the NPC. If you don't have the rank, the craftsmen are the way in — and they're not going anywhere.

docs.title: The stations
docs.text: Station Who runs it What it's for Basic Refinery Browntul Refining tier-1 ores, and making Ember Stones and Big Ingots Advanced Refinery Browntul Tier-2 ores and Blaze Cores Supreme Refinery Browntul Tier-3 ores and Fire Essence Master Refinery Browntul Tier-4 ores — the endgame metals Rusty Forge Velreal Common weapons Iron Forge Velreal Uncommon weapons Tempered Forge Velreal Rare weapons Runed Forge Velreal Epic weapons Mythic Forge Velreal Legendary weapons Padded Workbench Velreal Common armor Hardened Workbench Velreal Uncommon armor Plated Workbench Velreal Rare armor Runed Workbench Velreal Epic armor Ascended Workbench Velreal Legendary armor Apothecary Kiko Gem Catalysts — the gateway to all gem and enchant crafting Gem Station Kiko Stat gemstones Enchant Forge Kiko Enchant Stones Ability Gem Forge Kiko Your class's ability stones Cooking stations Kate Food, buffs — own section

docs.title: The refineries
docs.text:
Talk to Browntul.

Raw ore is useless until it's refined. There are four refineries, one per mine tier, and each only handles the ores from its own tier.

Refinery Level Yield Fuel it burns Fuel it makes Basic 1 1 ore → 3 ingots Ember Stone Ember Stone Advanced 15 1 ore → 3 ingots Blaze Core Blaze Core Supreme 30 1 ore → 2 ingots Fire Essence Fire Essence Master 45 1 ore → 2 ingots All three at once —

The chain matters: each refinery produces the fuel the next one up needs, so you can never skip a tier. Supreme is where yields drop from three to two and materials start getting genuinely scarce.

Master Refinery is expensive

A single Master refine costs 4 Ember Stones, 4 Blaze Cores and 8 Fire Essences on top of the ore, and takes 12 seconds. Start stockpiling reagents long before you reach level 45.

The Basic Refinery is also where you make Big Ingots — six ingots plus two Ember Stones compress into one. See Ores & Materials for why those matter.

Every refine awards both Smelting and Blacksmithing experience.

docs.title: Forges and workbenches
docs.text:
Talk to Velreal.

These don't create items from nothing — they upgrade an item you already have. You bring the base weapon or armor piece plus metal, and get back a crafted version with better, rolled stats.

There's a forge and a workbench for each rarity, and which one you use is decided by the rarity of the item you're upgrading.

docs.title: Weapons
docs.text:
Fifteen weapon types are supported: Sword, Great Sword, Katana, Dagger, Gauntlet, Spear, Axe, Great Axe, Hammer, Great Hammer, Staff, Wand, Bow, Crossbow and Shield.

Every weapon has its own signature metal pair — you can't substitute:

Weapon Metals Weapon Metals Sword Nightsteel + Sunsteel Great Axe Abyssium + Mystical Molten Alloy Great Sword Nightsteel + Starsteel Hammer Sunsteel + Mystical Molten Alloy Katana Nightsteel + Froststeel Great Hammer Starsteel + Mystical Molten Alloy Dagger Abyssium + Nightsteel Staff Sunsteel + Starsteel Gauntlet Abyssium + Froststeel Wand Sunsteel + Froststeel Spear Starsteel + Froststeel Bow Abyssium + Starsteel Axe Nightsteel + Mystical Molten Alloy Crossbow Abyssium + Sunsteel Shield Mystical Molten Alloy + Froststeel

docs.title: Armor
docs.text:
Four pieces — Helmet, Chestplate, Leggings, Boots — each craftable in five ways:

Recipe Result Plain Rolls a random archetype Arcane Locked to Arcane Deadeye Locked to Deadeye Reinforced Locked to Reinforced Savage Locked to Savage

That's the whole design: the plain recipe gambles on archetype, and the four named recipes let you guarantee the archetype you want by paying a different metal pair instead. Same cost, different metals — so what really gates your build is which ores you've stockpiled.

docs.title: Base versus "+"
docs.text:
• Base grade uses regular ingots in bulk — 18 to 48 of each metal, depending on the weapon's size.
  • "+" grade uses Big Ingots — only two to five of each — plus Gold Ingots instead of Ember Stones, and awards more Blacksmithing experience.

Craft times run 5–10 seconds for weapons; armor is consistent by slot at 6 seconds for helmets and boots, 8 for leggings, 9 for chestplates.

docs.title: Gems and enchanting
docs.text:
Talk to Kiko.

Four stations feed into this, and the order matters:

Apothecary  →  Gem Catalyst  ─┬─→  Gem Station    (stat gemstones)
                              └─→  Enchant Forge  (enchant stones)

Ability Gem Forge  —  separate system, no catalyst needed

The Apothecary has exactly one recipe, and everything it consumes is a dungeon reagent. If you're wondering why you can't make gems, the answer is almost always that you haven't run dungeons for materials.

The Gem Station makes stat gemstones in four families and five quality grades. The Enchant Forge makes Enchant Stones — 123 of them, covering both Runaria's custom enchantments and vanilla ones, several at levels above the vanilla ceiling. Both award Gemforging experience.

The Ability Gem Forge is separate. It crafts the five levels of your class's signature ability, and it's gated by class — you only ever see recipes for the class you're currently playing, so the menu looks small even though it's one of the largest on the server.

See Gems & Enchanting for the detail.

docs.title: Cooking stations
docs.text:
Talk to Kate to get started.

Cooking doesn't work like the stations on this page. Rather than opening a station at an NPC, you buy the furniture and place it in your own kitchen — four different stations, each doing a different job, and 120 dishes across them.

It's a large enough system to have its own section.

docs.title: Which profession does what
docs.text:
Profession Fed by Smelting Refineries only Blacksmithing Refineries, all forges, all workbenches Gemforging Gem Station and Enchant Forge Cooking The four cooking stations

Blacksmithing and Gemforging both award experience on the same ladder — more for higher-rarity work — so the rarity you're working at matters more than the number of crafts.

docs.title: Guilds
docs.text: Create a guild for free, claim territory, bank money together, buy 16 guild upgrades, and climb the fame ladder from rank F to S by completing guild quest contracts.

docs.title: Creating & joining
docs.text:
• /guild opens the guild menu. Guildless players see Create and Browse. Creation is free — pick a name (max 24 characters) and a tag (max 4). Guilds start with 10 member slots.
  • Guilds can be Open (join instantly), Request (apply via the guild's inbox), or Closed (hidden from the list).
  • Roles run Member → Trusted → Admin → Leader. Leaders customise exactly what each role can do — build, deposit, claim land, manage members, and so on. Withdrawing from the bank is leader-only by default.
  • Your guild tag automatically appears in front of your name in chat.

docs.title: Guild bank & land claims
docs.text:
The guild bank funds everything. Claims, upgrades, and customisation are all paid from the bank, not your personal wallet. Deposit or withdraw in 1k / 10k / 100k / custom amounts.

Three ways to claim land:

  1. The golden-shovel wand — set two corners and a live glowing outline previews the claim.
  2. A centred claim — a 128×128 square around where you stand.
  3. A chunk claim — just the 16×16 chunk you're in.

Type confirm in chat to buy the previewed claim, or cancel to back out. You're only charged on confirm.

  • Cost is 1.5 per block — a chunk costs 384, a full 128×128 claim about 24,600.
  • Claims draw from a block budget (base 16,384 blocks total across all claims, expandable with the Expanded Borders upgrade). You can make unlimited numbers of claims, but each new one must touch your existing territory in that world. The first claim in a world can go anywhere.
  • Claims can't overlap another guild's land or a protected region.
  • Entering guild land shows an "Entering [TAG] Land" title. Outsiders can't build, interact, or open containers on your claims.
  • Unclaim by standing in a claim and shift-clicking. There's no refund, so claim deliberately.

Guild home: one per guild. Teleport with /guild home or the bed icon in the hub.

docs.title: Fame & prestige (F → S)
docs.text:
Fame comes from guild quest contracts.

Rank Fame required F starting rank E 1,000 D 3,000 C 7,500 B 15,000 A 30,000 S 60,000
  • Rank passive: every rank above F gives the whole guild +2% class EXP, up to +12% at S.
  • Renowned bonus: the top 3 guilds on the fame board get an extra +5% / +3% / +2%.
  • Daily streak: complete 3+ guild quests in a day to build a streak worth +5% fame per day, capped at +25%. A day with zero quests resets it; 1–2 quests holds it. Days roll over at 3:00 AM ET.
  • Weekend Rush: all guild-quest fame is ×1.5 on Saturday and Sunday.

Fame decay at rank B and above

Once your guild reaches rank B, you must complete at least one guild quest every 7 days. Miss that window and the guild drops a full rank, then keeps bleeding fame each further questless day until it falls below B. Members are warned at login when 2 days or fewer remain.

The Sabbatical Charter upgrade pauses decay for 7 days, on a 30-day cooldown.

The #1 guild's leader is immortalised on the Champion Monument NPC at The Market.

docs.title: Guild upgrades
docs.text:
Sixteen upgrades bought from the guild bank (requires the Manage Settings role permission), each gated behind a prestige rank.

docs.title: Quests & Quest Points
docs.text: Three layers of quests: a story line that introduces the server, a daily quest board with 300 quests and its own shop currency, and guild quest boards that feed your guild's fame.

docs.title: The story line
docs.text:
Eight quests played in order, starting automatically for every new player:

Welcome to Runaria → All About Classes → Meet Sylari's Citizens → Creating a Guild → The Sacred Garden → What Are Traits → What Are Skills → What Are Attributes

They introduce every major system through NPC dialogue and pay money and skill points along the way.

Priest Caelen also offers one daily quest — End- and undead-themed — once you're a few story quests in. Each completion pays 500 money and deepens your relationship with him.

docs.title: The daily quest board
docs.text:
Open it by clicking a Quest Board in a town, or with /dailyquests. It's a quest log, not a pick-one board — you take several quests at once.

  • Board slots grow with your lifetime quest points: 9 slots to start, +1 per 10 lifetime points, capped at 27.
  • Quest rarity improves as your lifetime points grow — from mostly Common draws at zero points to a healthy spread of Rare, Epic, and Legendary at 150+.
  • 3 board refreshes per day, and you earn them: clear every quest on your board and you can claim a whole new one. The quest day rolls over at 3:00 AM ET.
  • All 300 daily quests are kill or delivery quests, and every one ends with Kael — she's where rewards are collected.

docs.title: Quest points & Quest Boxes
docs.text:
Every daily quest pays 1 spendable quest point.

Two different point counters

Your lifetime quest point score only unlocks board slots and better rarities. Your spendable points are the shop currency. Spending never reduces your lifetime score, so it can't cost you board slots or leaderboard rank.

Dailies also drop Quest Boxes — loot boxes you carry as items.

  • Left-click to preview the full loot table with real odds. Right-click to open.
  • Common / Uncommon / Rare quests give 1 / 2 / 3 common boxes. Epic / Legendary give 1 / 2 uncommon boxes.
  • Boxes contain gear, ingots, seeds, potions, gemstones, money bundles, skill and attribute points, rare Class Tokens — and very rare rolls of any of the 33 Bots or 10 Backpacks.

docs.title: The Quest Shop
docs.text:
/questshop spends your points.

Item Price Daily limit Common Quest Box 12 pts — Uncommon Quest Box 40 pts 2 Class Token 75 pts 1 Small Health Potion ×8 6 pts — Small Mana Potion ×8 6 pts — Assorted Seeds ×4 5 pts — Cracked Ruby Gemstone 20 pts — $10,000 8 pts 5 Hunting Backpack (14–22 slots) 50 pts 1

docs.title: Guild quest boards
docs.text:
Served from the guild menu, not an NPC.

  • Your guild's rank decides how many contracts are offered per cycle. You run one at a time — more with the Ambitious Endeavors upgrade.
  • Progress is shared across the guild, and completion pays guild fame + guild bank money, plus an MVP bonus (an item or a skill/attribute point) for the top contributor.
  • Rewards scale steeply with rank: an F-board quest pays ~20 fame and 1,000 bank; an S-board quest pays ~800 fame and 60,000 bank.
  • Board refreshes are earned by finishing the whole assignment — base 5 per day, up to 20 with upgrades.
  • The Contract Broker NPC sells 8 extra daily-rerolled contracts for guild bank money.

Fame or points, never both

Guild quests award fame, not quest points. Daily quests award points, not fame.

The board GUI also holds leaderboards for lifetime points earned and dailies completed. Both rank on lifetime totals, so spending in the shop never drops your placing.

docs.title: Farming & Seasons
docs.text: Runaria replaces vanilla farming with a seasonal system. Crops grow only in their season, need watering, and roll a quality grade when harvested.

docs.title: Seasons
docs.text:
Four seasons rotate automatically — Spring → Summer → Autumn → Winter — each lasting 28 in-game days, or roughly 9 hours of real time. A full year takes about a day and a half.

  • Planting a crop out of season is refused outright.
  • If the season turns while a crop is in the ground, it simply stops growing. It does not die.
  • Farming is disabled in the spawn world — plant elsewhere.

Greenhouse Glass beats the calendar

Greenhouse Glass within 5 blocks lets a crop grow in any season. That's the real reason to build a greenhouse: not protection from winter, but the ability to farm a Spring crop in Autumn and keep every plot productive year-round.

docs.title: What actually kills crops
docs.text:
Crows. That's it.

Seasons don't kill anything on Runaria — an out-of-season crop just sits there until its season comes round again, or until you glass it in. Scarecrows protect crops within 7 blocks from crows, and a scarecrow plus greenhouse glass makes a plot effectively safe.

docs.title: How growth works
docs.text:
A crop only makes progress while its conditions are met. Two things are checked as it grows:

  1. Season — must be one the crop accepts, unless Greenhouse Glass is covering it.
  2. Water — the farmland has to stay hydrated. Tree and fruit crops are thirstier than field crops.

Runaria uses ordinary vanilla farmland, so the usual rules apply: keep water within range of your plot, or bring it to the crops yourself with a watering can or a sprinkler. Rain waters your fields for free. Dry farmland won't kill a crop, but it will stall it.

docs.title: Star quality
docs.text:
Every harvest rolls a grade:

Grade Base chance Normal 85% Silver Star 10% Golden Star 5%

Quality fertilizer shifts those odds substantially:

Fertilizer Normal / Silver / Golden Quality I 70% / 20% / 10% Quality II 55% / 30% / 15% Quality III 40% / 40% / 20%

Star crops aren't just worth more — cooking carries their quality straight through to the plate, and a handful of the best dishes won't accept anything less. See Cooking.

docs.title: Seeds and rarity
docs.text:
Every crop has a rarity, and rarity is what decides how hard its seed is to come by. Seeds come from Seed Bags, which roll three times each.

Rarity Seeds in the pool Chance of any seed of this tier, per bag Chance of one specific seed, per bag Common 9 87.5% 15.8% Uncommon 6 57.8% 12.0% Rare 6 36.4% 6.8% Epic 5 20.9% 4.4% Legendary 4 8.7% 2.2% Unique 1 1.5% 1.5%

Reading those numbers

The last column is the one that matters when you're hunting a particular crop. Chasing Lychee specifically is roughly a 1-in-67 bag, while any given Common seed turns up in about one bag in six.

Seeds can also be bought from the server shop, which restocks a small rotating selection every three hours — weighted so common seeds appear far more often than rare ones.

Peach (Spring–Autumn, 1–5 yield, 6 XP) and Apple (any season, 1–4 yield, 3 XP) don't appear in Seed Bags. Apple is a tree that keeps producing once established, and neither rolls star grades.

What to plant

Durian and Red Packet give the most farming experience by a wide margin. Grape, Dragon Fruit and Apple are the slowest growers. And because Greenhouse Glass frees you from the calendar, the practical question is less "what's in season" than "what's worth the plot".

Apply order matters

Quality, Speed Grow and Yield Increase must go on before you plant. Soil Retain can be applied at any time.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
/attributes opens the attribute menu. You earn 2 attribute points per class level — about 198 by level 100.

You cannot fill the tree

There are 36 attributes with 532 points between them, and you will only ever earn around 198. You can fill roughly 37% of the tree. Attributes are a genuine build choice, not a checklist — spend them deliberately.

Respeccing costs an attribute reallocation point.
